newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht up, interbank rate down in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht up, interbank rate down in late trade.

text.p: The baht edged up against the dollar in quiet, late trade on Wednesday reflecting the U.S. unit's weakness abroad, dealers said.
The baht was trading at 26.080/26.085 late compared with 26.085/26.095 earlier.
"The baht firmed against the dollar in line with the greenback's trend abroad. The market was very quiet as Singaporean players were reluctant to take positions," said one dealer at a European bank.
The midrate was fixed at 26.09 per dollar against 26.07 on Friday. Markets were closed on Monday and Tuesday.
The overnight interbank rate fell to 8.25-8.50 percent in late trade from 9.00-9.50 in the morning on rising liquidity, dealers said.
"Some local banks were lending their surplus funds in the afternoon. There were very few borrowers in the market today," said one money market dealer.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was down to 5.50/6.00 satangs per dollar late compared with 6.75/7.50 on Friday.
